transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
The U.S. military has returned all of its long-range bomber station at a British airbase
back to the United States.
NPR's Greg Myry reports this comes just a week after British authorities arrested and
briefly detained five men with suspected ties to Iran near the base.
The U.S. military says all the bombers at Britain's Fairford airbase in the southwest
part of the country have returned to their home bases.
Vice President J.D. Vance said the move was made out of an abundance of caution.
He also referred to Iranian acts of terrorism against U.S. targets in the past, but did
not offer details on any new threats.
The U.S. has used the base to carry out airstrikes in the war against Iran.
Just over a week ago, British police arrested five young men near the base, raising suspicions
the facility might be a target.
However, the five have all been released on bail.
Greg Myry, NPR News, Washington.
With less than a month to go before the midterm elections, Republican super PACs have canceled
millions of dollars of planned spending in North Carolina's U.S. Senate race, NPR's Stephen
Fowler reports some of the money is being redirected to an unexpectedly competitive race
in Kansas.
According to ad tracking firm Ad Impact, more than $16 million in future reservations for
North Carolina's Senate race have been canceled since Friday.
Polls show the Democratic candidate Roy Cooper with a sizable lead there over the Republican
Michael Watley.
Some of that money has been redirected to the Senate race in Kansas.
It's one of many Midwestern states where rising fuel costs and Trump administration policies
like tariffs have hit hardest and where enough voters say they've soured on Republicans to
make these reliably red states competitive.
Stephen Fowler, NPR News.
Brazil's presidential election heads to a runoff later this month.
The right made significant gains in yesterday's national vote.
Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of Brazil's former far-right president, outperformed the country's
veteran leftist incumbent Luis Inacilula da Silva.
And Pierre's carry con has more.
Flavio Bolsonaro won with 47 percent of the vote.
He's the 45 year old eldest son of Jair Bolsonaro, who was barred from running this time.
He was convicted of flooding a coup to overturn the 2022 election.
The current president, who is 80 years old, Lula, received 45 percent of the vote.
NPR's Carrie Khan reporting.
Former Speaker of the House Dennis Hastert has died at the age of 84.
The former Illinois lawmaker was the longest serving Republican Speaker of the House.
After leaving office, he admitted in court to having sexually abused teenage boys during
his years as a high school wrestling coach.
He would be sentenced then to 15 years in federal prison for hush money payments to
cover up those crimes.
From Washington, this is NPR News.
A school bus carrying dozens of high school students was involved in a deadly collision
early this morning in Winterhaven, Florida.
Hoe County Sheriff Grady Judd says for unknown reasons, a white Chevy Malibu veered into
traffic traveling in the opposite direction, struck the bus and set off a chain reaction
of collisions involving multiple vehicles.
It was a terrible tragic morning.
We had a beautiful 10th grade girl lose her life.
She was in the bus.
The sheriff says one person in a Jeep was also killed.
Multiple people were injured.
The United Kingdom's Green Party has declared Zionism as a form of racism, and Pierre's
Daniel Lesterin reports from Tel Aviv that the Green Party leader is now barred from
entering Israel.
The left-wing Green Party in the UK passed the motion at a party conference Sunday.
The motion says the Green Party opposes Zionism, the ideological movement behind the creation
of Israel as a Jewish state.
The party said Zionism is an ethno-nationalist political project.
They called for Israel to be replaced by a single democratic state, including the occupied
Palestinian territories.
The Green Party is the only major UK party with a Jewish leader.
The Israeli foreign ministry has now declared him a persona non grata in Israel.
Israel said the Green Party's motion is anti-Semitic, that it calls for the destruction of Israel,
and that it goes beyond the boundaries of legitimate political debate.
Daniel Lesterin, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
I'm Lakshmi Singh in PR News, in Washington.
